Self-Awareness & Self-Understanding

Q01 When I notice a change in how I feel, I can usually recognise what may have contributed to it.

Never · What you could work on

Try What happened just before a recent change in how you felt?

Possible benefit Spot what tends to shift your mood.

Q02 When making a decision, I can tell whether I am being influenced more by my feelings or by the facts.

Rarely · What you could work on

Try Think of one decision. Which feelings and facts influenced it?

Possible benefit See what is driving a decision.

Q03 When I react strongly to something, I find it difficult to understand why.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try Recall a strong reaction. What might have been behind it?

Possible benefit Recognise what tends to set off a strong reaction.

Q04 I can tell when something from my past is affecting how I react today.

Often · What seems to support you

Try Did a past experience shape a recent response?

Possible benefit Notice when a past experience is shaping the present.

Q05 After an argument or disagreement, I think about whether I could have handled things differently.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try After a disagreement, what would you keep or change next time?

Possible benefit Find one change to try in the next disagreement.

Q06 When something happens, I try to understand the facts before making assumptions about it.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What could you ask before reaching a conclusion?

Possible benefit Reach conclusions with more context.

Thinking Patterns & Mental Flexibility

Q07 I keep thinking about past mistakes or problems, even when I know I cannot change what happened.

Often · What you could work on

Try Which thought keeps returning? Is there something you can act on now?

Possible benefit Separate something you can act on from a thought that keeps repeating.

Q08 When things don't happen as I expected, I try to look at the situation in different ways.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What is one other way to understand a recent disappointment?

Possible benefit See options you may have missed at first.

Q09 When I make a mistake, I blame myself and keep thinking negatively about it.

Rarely · What seems to support you

Try What would you say to a friend who made the same mistake?

Possible benefit Respond to a mistake with more kindness and perspective.

Q10 When I learn something new, I am willing to change my opinion if needed.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try What new information might change your view?

Possible benefit Make room to update your view as you learn.

Q11 When I don't know what will happen, I often expect the worst.

Rarely · What seems to support you

Try Which parts of an uncertain situation are facts, and which are predictions?

Possible benefit Distinguish what you know from what you fear might happen.

Q12 When my first approach to solving a problem doesn't work, I try a different way.

Often · What seems to support you

Try If your first approach does not work, what else could you try?

Possible benefit Find another way forward when the first plan stalls.

Emotional Balance & Response Management

Q13 When I get angry, I take a moment to calm myself before reacting.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What could help you pause during a difficult conversation?

Possible benefit Create space to choose how you respond.

Q14 When I am upset, I say or do things that I later regret.

Often · What you could work on

Try What did you notice just before a reaction you later regretted?

Possible benefit Notice an early cue to pause before responding.

Q15 I can accept feeling worried or upset without needing to fix everything immediately.

Rarely · What you could work on

Try Can you name a feeling without deciding what to do about it yet?

Possible benefit Give yourself time before deciding what to do about a feeling.

Q16 When something upsets or disappoints me, I find it difficult to focus on my usual activities afterward.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What helps you return to one everyday task after feeling upset?

Possible benefit Identify one manageable way to return to your routine.

Q17 When I feel very stressed or upset, I do something that helps me calm down and handle the situation better.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try What has helped you feel calmer in a difficult moment?

Possible benefit Have a familiar way to settle yourself when stressed.

Q18 When I feel upset with someone, I can explain how I feel without shouting or blaming them.

Often · What seems to support you

Try How would you describe a feeling using “I feel…”?

Possible benefit Make it easier for someone to understand how you feel.

Decision-Making & Behavioural Control

Q19 Before making an important decision, I think about how it might affect me or others.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try Who might be affected by a decision you are considering?

Possible benefit See who could be affected before you decide.

Q20 I sometimes make decisions too quickly and later regret not thinking them through.

Rarely · What seems to support you

Try What information would you want before a similar decision?

Possible benefit Give yourself time to check a detail that matters.

Q21 I delay making important decisions because I am afraid of making the wrong choice.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What is one small part of a delayed decision you could clarify?

Possible benefit Make a delayed decision feel more manageable.

Q22 Even when I am unsure about the outcome, I take steps toward achieving my goals.

Often · What seems to support you

Try What manageable step could you take without knowing every outcome?

Possible benefit Make a start when the outcome is uncertain.

Q23 Even when I realise that a decision may be wrong, I find it difficult to change my mind.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try What would help you reconsider a choice that no longer fits?

Possible benefit Make it easier to adjust when a choice stops fitting.

Q24 The decisions I make in my daily life usually match what is important to me.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try What matters most to you in your next decision?

Possible benefit Choose a next step that fits your priorities.

Often · What seems to support you

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Q29 When I realise that my words or actions have hurt someone, I can accept my mistake.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Q30 I can say no when someone asks me to do something I am not comfortable with.

Often · What seems to support you

Stress Coping, Resilience & Personal Growth

Q31 When I face a difficult problem, I can usually figure out what to do next.

Sometimes · What you reported sometimes

Try Which part of a current challenge feels manageable?

Possible benefit Turn an overwhelming problem into one doable action.

Q32 I keep worrying about things even when I know they are outside my control.

Often · What you could work on

Q33 When things don't go as planned, I can adjust and find another way forward.

Almost Always · What seems to support you

Try What alternative could you explore when a plan changes?

Q34 When I feel stressed, I find it difficult to take proper care of myself.

Rarely · What seems to support you

Try Which everyday need would you like to make room for today?

Q35 When I face a difficult situation, I am comfortable asking others for help.

Often · What seems to support you

Try Who could you ask for a specific kind of help?

Almost Always · What seems to support you

About this reflection

Innerly V1 uses 36 questions in six categories. No scoring key or clinical thresholds were supplied with this questionnaire, so this report describes responses without calculating a total score or diagnosis. Earlier questionnaire reports keep their original questions and cannot be compared directly.

Each dimension keeps its six original questions. The response map and detail views use your exact choices, without averaging or reverse-scoring. Over time shows one question across up to eight actual check-ins in the same questionnaire language. A change is not evidence of improvement, deterioration or a treatment effect.

Question language: English. Translations are editorial and have not been independently validated.
